erin: quick sync — hit a tricky behavior in staging where a reserved pool drain + burst lane caused sustained p99 regression for a tenant.
lee: ugh, details?
erin: sequence was: operator started draining nodes for a maintenance patch -> reserved capacity for tenant dropped from 20 -> 5 -> 0 over ~3min -> controller routed requests into burst lane -> burst lane is CPU-backed, so tail latency spiked.
noah: are we talking about graceful degradation or an implementation bug in routing?
erin: leaning degradation+race. routing fallback picks any compatible variant, but we don't currently check p99 impact before switching. fallback is binary: if reserved "unavailable" -> route to burst.
sophia: can we add a throttled admission step? like a short-circuit that samples a small % to the burst lane first and measures p50/p99 before full spillover?
noah: yes, sampling would help. Also we lack a clear "degrade mode" signal in the operator API. Right now operator sends "unavailable" which equals immediate spill.
ops-bot: incident created: #INC-4527 for staging p99 regression :rotating_light:
erin: propose a two-tier fallback policy:
1) soft-fallback (sampling): route 5-10% of inflight requests to fallback variant and monitor p50/p95/p99 for X seconds.
2) fast-fallback: if metrics within thresholds, ramp to 100% over a short window.
3) emergency-cutover: if sampling shows catastrophic latency, reject / NACK with standardized error (so callers can fallback to cached or offline path).
lee: thresholds? what are safe defaults?
sophia: suggest p99 < 2x reserved p99 and p50 < 1.5x during sampling, and error rate delta < 0.5% absolute.
noah: can we implement as operator policy with params:

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  sampling_rate: 0.05
  sampling_window_s: 30
  p99_multiplier_threshold: 2.0
  p50_multiplier_threshold: 1.5
  error_rate_delta_threshold: 0.005
  ramp_up_steps: [25, 50, 100]
```

sophia: that looks good. where should the policy live? tenant config or cluster-level?
erin: tenant-level makes sense for per-customer SLOs, cluster-level default for org-wide safety.
noah: operator boundary question: who owns the sampling telemetry? operator should emit a "fallback_evaluation" metric with tags {tenant, fallback_variant, sample_rate}. Control plane (or console) will read it and decide whether to continue.
lee: exposing metrics is fine. we also need an API hook for manual abort and for the console to override the ramp.
erin: API sketch:

POST /operator/v1/reservations/{id}/fallback/evaluate
body: {"policy": <policy-json>, "mode": "start|abort|promote"}

response 202 with evaluation_id

sophia: add GET /operator/v1/evaluations/{evaluation_id}/status

noah: note: keep RBAC scoped to platform/tenant-admin. we'll gate abort/promote.
sophia: testing plan: unit for admission sampler, integration test in local cluster that simulates reserved drain, loadgen to validate ramp behavior, and chaos run in staging.
erin: we should also add a safety circuit to prevent oscillation: if a tenant toggles between reserved and fallback within <60s more than 3 times, disable automatic fallback and surface to ops.
lee: add metric fallback_oscillation_count and a prometheus alert.
ops-bot: action items created: #TASK-331 (implement policy schema + operator API), #TASK-332 (metrics + console UX), #TASK-333 (integration + chaos run).
erin: who picks up TASK-331? noah can you own operator changes?
noah: I can take it. I'll draft the CR and proto for the API by EOD tomorrow.
sophia: I'll wire up the console override buttons and the alert rule — + add a small UX note about expected behavior.
lee: I'll own the integration/chaos tests with loadgen scenarios.
erin: thanks. let's also add a short note to the autoscale RFC followup doc with the policy sketch and link INC-4527 for context.
noah: ack. I'll post a brief PR in the RFC repo once the API proto is done.
erin: cool. small follow-up: should fallback ever route to a smaller GPU variant instead of CPU-only? preference is yes but we need packing guarantees.
sophia: implement ordering in fallback_policy.fallback_order: [gpu-small, cpu-only], and operator will only pick gpu-small if cluster has available slices. if not, move down list.
lee: sounds good. ok team, thanks. will follow up in PRs. :thumbsup:
